solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Repeated phrase always employed by human traffickers

indicators.note: the letters are put to use by the words human traffickers, sitting inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: A slogan that people smugglers always use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' sits between the definition and the indicator to smooth the surface: a phrase used over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred syllable or slogan chanted over and over in meditation is exactly a repeated phrase.

clue.text: Model heading off for Spanish region

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the synonym for model is taken away

parts.note: a model of virtue is a paragon, a perfect example

explanation.surface: A fashion model heads off to a region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic kingdom in north-east Spain, now one of its autonomous communities.

clue.text: Astaire, say, departs having broken cane in silly part

indicators.note: the departure letter and the broken cane go inside the scrambled part
silly suggests the word part is mixed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of cane are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Fred Astaire walks off after snapping his cane while playing a silly role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cane' and 'part' look like props and roles in the surface; 'silly' and 'broken' are both anagram signals, and 'in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the most famous example of a performer whose feet tap out rhythms.

clue.text: Everyone agreed about carbon, suddenly

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: the word for agreed goes around the carbon symbol

parts.note: people who agree are at one
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A group suddenly reaches consensus about carbon emissions.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something happening abruptly, all in one moment.

clue.text: Plain flat? Small play on words

parts.note: a flat is where one lives, one's home
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a flat is plain, then makes a small joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an adjective next to 'Plain' but is the noun for a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Homely, unsophisticated and simple in style, as cloth woven at home once was.

clue.text: Fiery type in Proust novel going after husband

indicators.note: the scrambled author's name comes after the letter for husband

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of Proust are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A passionate character in a Proust novel goes after her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Percy, nicknamed this, is the hot-headed rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1; 'going after' puts H before the anagram OTSPUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a rash, hot-tempered person, after Shakespeare's impetuous Harry Percy.

clue.text: Landed estate's custom, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so a word sounding like the one for custom is entered

parts.note: a custom or way of doing things is a manner

explanation.surface: The traditions of a landed estate, as people tell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A country house with its lands, historically held by a lord.

clue.text: Fool is up for a form of protest

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nit, short for nitwit, is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool stands up for a kind of protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters occupying a place and refusing to leave stage this kind of demonstration.

clue.text: Relatives, American, in the US government

parts.note: uncles are relatives

explanation.surface: Family members and an American working in the US government.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in a top hat is the traditional personification of the American federal state.

clue.text: A politician in public house allowed to give handout

indicators.note: the article and politician sit inside the abbreviation for a pub

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for a public house
MP is a Member of Parliament
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: An MP in a pub is permitted to hand out leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: A small printed leaflet given out free is a handout.

clue.text: Become aware of warning

definitions.meaning: advance word, as in giving a week's warning before leaving

explanation.surface: Someone spots a warning sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to observe; the noun means formal notification or warning.

clue.text: Garbo, wickedly, beginning to tease famous actor

indicators.note: wickedly suggests the letters of Garbo are treated badly, so jumbled
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Greta Garbo wickedly starts to tease a famous film actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey, star of Casablanca, is one of Hollywood's best-known leading men.

clue.text: Mountain range, extremely pretty and uncommonly serene

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters of serene are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A mountain range described as very pretty and unusually serene.
explanation.definitionFit: The range forms the border between France and Spain.

clue.text: Supernatural being appearing in Angel Falls

indicators.note: the letters show up inside the words Angel Falls, across the space

explanation.surface: A spirit is seen at Angel Falls, the Venezuelan waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous creature of folklore is a supernatural being.

clue.text: Changed frock later on for one like Svengali?

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of frock later on are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone changes their dress later, perhaps on a controlling person's orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the manipulative hypnotist in du Maurier's Trilby, is an example of someone who must dominate others.

clue.text: Guard to see later

parts.note: to look is to see
after means later

explanation.surface: A security guard says they will see someone later.
explanation.definitionFit: To take care of and protect someone, as a guardian does.

clue.text: A system set up by the police may show two artists parking without charge

definitions.text: A system set up by the police

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the two artists go around the charge

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual abbreviation for an artist; two of them give RA twice
to charge is to rush forward, to dart
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A police setup catches two artists parking for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without charge' reads as free of charge, but 'without' means outside, putting DART between the two RAs.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed check using radio waves, set up by police to catch speeding drivers.

clue.text: Surrey air?

definitions.meaning: a surrey is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle, as in the song about one with a fringe on top
air in the sense of bearing, the way one holds oneself

explanation.surface: It poses as a question about the air in Surrey, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is also an English county south of London, the reading the surface pushes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a horse-drawn vehicle and a person's posture or bearing.

clue.text: Opera singer had unfortunately aged

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of singer had are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
aged means old

explanation.surface: An opera singer has, sadly, grown old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opera singer' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Opera' alone; 'unfortunately' gives DASRHEING from SINGER HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's opera opening his Ring cycle, about the Rhine gold stolen by Alberich.

clue.text: Gardening tool in meadow initially overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

explanation.surface: A garden tool left lying in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is the fodder: in = at home, HOME, less the M that starts 'meadow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled tool with a blade for weeding and loosening soil.

clue.text: Irritated — wanted to catch learner driver

indicators.note: the word for wanted holds, or catches, the learner's letter

parts.note: wanted means needed
L is the plate a British learner driver displays

explanation.surface: Someone was annoyed and wanted to catch a learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: To be provoked or annoyed by persistent jibes, as if pricked.

clue.text: Speak, after end of championship, in golf club

indicators.note: the word for speak comes after the final letter
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: A player speaks after the end of a championship at their golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' suggests a clubhouse; here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat-faced club used for rolling the ball on the green.

clue.text: Heartless article about party animals makes one cross

indicators.note: the trimmed article goes around the party animals
heartless means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: the definite article is the
ravers are people who party hard

explanation.surface: A cruel article about partygoers makes someone angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry; it is the verb, to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over or across something, such as a mountain slope.

clue.text: Ill-defined fever following first of vaccinations

indicators.note: the fever comes after the first letter
the first letter of the word

parts.note: ague is an old word for a fever, especially malarial

explanation.surface: A vague fever follows the first round of vaccinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclear and imprecise, without definite outline.

clue.text: Citrus fruit, not round variety

indicators.note: not means the round letter is left out of the fruit

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A citrus fruit that isn't a round variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of goods is a variety of them.

clue.text: Area to decorate round university's central hall

indicators.note: the word for decorate goes round the university letter

parts.note: to trim is to decorate

explanation.surface: An area to decorate around a university's central hall.
explanation.definitionFit: An open central court or hall in a Roman house or modern building.

clue.text: Leave name on pot in specialist language

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the pot

parts.note: a jar is a pot
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a name label on a pot in technical terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms used by a particular profession that outsiders find hard to follow.

clue.text: Learned line to say again

parts.note: to iterate is to repeat, to say again

explanation.surface: A scholar learns a line by repeating it.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated and well read, able to read and write.

clue.text: Member of the clergy never terribly overdrawn?

indicators.note: terribly suggests things are badly arranged, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
an overdrawn account is in the red

explanation.surface: A vicar who is never badly overdrawn, it hints with a question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' shuffles NEVER together with RED, from 'overdrawn' (in the red).
explanation.definitionFit: A title and general term for a priest or minister.

clue.text: Rumour about harbour

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Gossip about a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour is a piece of hearsay, a report of something unconfirmed.
